title: Spurious-Correlation Traps: When Does Weak-to-Strong Generalization Inherit a Shortcut?

original_idea.body:
# Spurious-Correlation Traps: When Does Weak-to-Strong Generalization Inherit a Shortcut?

**Problem:** Recent work asks whether weak-to-strong generalization happens under spurious correlations, finding the strong student can inherit the weak teacher's shortcut. The conditions (correlation strength, task) under which the shortcut transfers vs. is corrected are not mapped in an accessible, training-free way.

**Direction:** Without fine-tuning, simulate the dynamic in-context: give a strong model 'weak supervisor' labels on a task with a planted spurious cue (e.g. a keyword correlated with the label), then test on a counterfactual set where the cue is decorrelated. Measure whether the strong model follows the spurious cue (inherits the shortcut) or the true signal, as a function of cue strength in the supervisor's labels.

**Why it matters:** Spurious-cue inheritance is how weak supervision can silently corrupt a stronger model. A training-free in-context probe makes this studiable by beginners and is highly counterfactual (no fine-tuning, public data).

**Relevant context:** Does Weak-to-strong Generalization Happen under Spurious Correlations? (arXiv:2509.24005); OpenAI W2S (ICML 2024) strong student fits weak-teacher limitations. Scoped to in-context label-following rather than fine-tuning.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Probes how weak supervision silently corrupts a stronger model via shortcut inheritance; defensible chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: In-context spurious-cue probe, no fine-tuning; mentorable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused shortcut-vs-true-signal measurement as a function of cue strength.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Highly counterfactual: no fine-tuning, public data, model-organism-style probe labs underdo.

novelty.reasoning: W2S spurious correlation studied via training; in-context version may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: W2S-under-spurious-correlation exists in training setups; the in-context probe is plausibly novel.
